When the PM&C Reset bit goes high (from the I.T. system), the PM&C counts are reset. Note these counts are monitored by the I.T. system independently from the production counts that may be maintained separately within the PLC for other purposes (which is why it is held for an extra scan: to prevent overwriting by other counters before they are reset) If supplied, the Increment inputs will increment the Piece Count(s) by P_IncrementAmount for each rising edge.
Additionally, the current cycle time restarts at zero, to prevent cycle time from last shift from being accumulated (this means that the first cycle will be shorter than normal in most situations where a cycletime crosses a shift).
Note: Additionally reset of cycletime on shift edge prevents cycletime from last shift from being accumulated.
The tag BypassPalletOrBufferCnt is used in both Machining and Assembly Type Maps. The text Buffer Count is the Machining Side and the Bypass Pallet Count is the Assembly Side. There is No Bypass Pallet Count in Machining and there is No Buffer Count in Assembly.

This rung takes the Current Load Cycle Time (DINT) and adds the Different Time (DINT) calculated previously from the system clock difference (in units of ms).

The I.T. system reads this bit to verify that the communication with the control system is not disrupted. The bit is toggled by the controller between on and off in 20 second intervals. This bit should therefore toggle indefinitely.

Validate the Year / Month / Day

When the ClockSynch bit is on, this means that the I.T. System has updated the Date-Write Day/Month/Year and we must then set the PLC clock to coincide with this date at 3am.
Note: This logic relies on the interface address to this FB. If the addresses above L0 change, then this Network will no longer work. LB0 refers to the temp variable CurDT, first byte, LB1 is the second byte, etc. Once CurDT is built up from the I.T. Write Year/Date/Month PLUS the time of 3am (at which the ClockSynch is always sent), the clock is updated using SFC0. Note that this is independent of the state of the PLC clock before this operation.
